sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, with about 28% of the model's importance, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use goes up, especially above roughly 0.6.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises from none to one delinquency and then levels off at two or more.
Income and length of credit history each have a moderate to weak effect, with higher income and longer histories associated with lower predicted risk.
Utilization and past delinquencies interact strongly: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two delinquencies than for those with none.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with risk somewhat higher above about 0.44.
Age and the two anonymised application attributes have negligible effects, and the data do not settle whether feature_b matters at all.
Recent credit inquiries have at most a weak effect on the predictions.
